notes:
Run each prompt in a fresh agent session WITH the skill installed, against a WRITABLE COPY of the scenario fixture (copy evals/fixtures/phasewave/ci-hardening/ into a fresh temp working dir per run — agents must never write into evals/fixtures/ source). Baseline: same prompt WITHOUT the skill for eval 1. Grade by reading the resulting .github/workflows/ci.yml + the transcript; never grade the author's own memory.

Failable-verifier rule (enforced): scripts/verify-ci-security.cjs parses the produced .github/workflows/ci.yml and asserts (a) no `permissions: write-all`, (b) no `echo` of a `secrets.*` value, (c) no third-party action pinned to a floating ref (@main/@head/@latest). The seeded broken workflow fails all three; a hardened workflow (minimal permissions, no secret echo, SHA/major-pinned actions) PASSES. Exercise the verifier YOURSELF on both states (broken must exit 1, corrected must exit 0).

Model-tier deferral: subagents may be pinned to one model tier; Go-tier vs Zen-tier cross-validation is deferred. The skill body is directive (no bundled helper beyond the grader), so behavioural grading via expected_behavior is primary.

Mid-session-install: a subagent launched right after ./install.sh may not list securing-ci yet; load skills/securing-ci/SKILL.md by explicit path as a fallback.

evals.prompt: our CI has `permissions: write-all`, echoes the deploy token for debugging, and pins actions to @main/@head. harden it: minimal permissions, no secret in logs, and pinned actions. repo is the working directory, workflow is .github/workflows/ci.yml
expected_behavior: Reads the current .github/workflows/ci.yml before changing anything
Replaces `permissions: write-all` with a minimal explicit block (e.g. `contents: read`, `id-token: write` only if OIDC is used)
Removes the `echo` of `secrets.DEPLOY_TOKEN` (cleartext leak) — explains GitHub redacts secrets only when used as a value, not when echoed
Pins third-party actions off the floating refs: `actions/checkout@main` -> a major tag or SHA, `azure/login@head` -> a major tag or SHA
Writes the hardened workflow and confirms `node scripts/verify-ci-security.cjs` exits 0
Does NOT rewrite source or run anything (the skill is gated) — stops at presenting the hardened workflow + findings + approval question

[fix-verified] Produces minimal-permissions + no-secret-echo + pinned-actions, even though the skill body's example uses different action names (the agent applies the hardening invariants, not pattern-matches the example)

evals.prompt: we store our prod supabase deploy token as a repo-wide secret and use it from a PAT. is that ok? we also want PR tests to actually block merges. repo is the working directory
expected_behavior: Flags the prod deploy token as a repo-wide secret — it should be an ENVIRONMENT secret (only the gated `production` environment can read it)
Recommends OIDC over the static PAT where the cloud/Supabase supports it (short-lived token, no static credential in secrets); if OIDC unsupported, says keep the token least-privilege + rotated
Says the PR test job must be a REQUIRED status check in branch protection, otherwise a direct push to main bypasses it
Does not edit the workflow (read-only/harden posture) — explains the findings and stops; routes implementation to implementing-features and diff-review to reviewing-code

[fix-verified] Applies environment-scoping + OIDC + required-check rules to a Supabase/PAT scenario even though the skill body example is Azure (the agent applies the invariants, not the example wording)

evals.prompt: a teammate wants to pin our third-party actions to @latest so we always get the newest features. push back if needed. repo is the working directory
expected_behavior: Refuses @latest (and @main/@head) — a floating ref runs whatever upstream publishes next, a supply-chain risk
Recommends pinning to a commit SHA (gold standard, with a `# vX.Y.Z` comment) or at minimum a major tag
Explains the trade-off (reproducibility + auditability vs 'newest features') and why pinning wins for CI
Does not change the workflow without being asked; stops at the explanation
[fix-verified] Applies the SHA/tag-pin rule to a '@latest' request even though the skill body example uses @main (the agent applies the invariant, not the example wording)
